sections.label: NE and Income good faith
sections.summary: NE and Income acted in good faith to strengthen Income, and the Government has no concerns over Allianz's standing or suitability.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is important to recognise that NE and Income had acted in good faith and their objective of wanting to go into this deal was to do the right thing, which is to strengthen Income, so that it could do well to continue to do good.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: I would also like to reiterate that the Government does not have concerns over Allianz's standing or suitability to acquire a majority stake in Income.

sections.label: Insurance Act amendment for MCCY views
sections.summary: The Insurance Act does not expressly let MAS consider MCCY's views for co-op-linked insurers, so an amendment is proposed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: However, the Insurance Act does not expressly provide for MAS to consider MCCY's views in applications where the insurer is either a co-op or linked to a co-op.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We, therefore, propose to amend the Insurance Act to provide a clear statutory basis for MCCY's views to be considered in any approval involving such applications.

sections.label: Minister may withhold approval
sections.summary: The amendment lets the Minister-in-charge of MAS consider the CSA Minister's views and withhold approval if in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Given that insurance co-ops are a special category of insurers with a social mission, we are proposing to amend the Insurance Act to provide for the Minister-in-charge of MAS to consider the views of the Minister responsible for the administration of the Co-operative Societies Act (CSA), to withhold approval involving such applications if the Minister-in-charge of MAS considers that it is in the public interest to do so.

sections.label: S$1.85 billion capital reduction transfer
sections.summary: The transaction involved a S$1.85 billion cash transfer from Income to proposed shareholders, unacceptable given Income's 2022 exemption from section 88 of the CSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In Monday's Ministerial Statement, a critical piece of information was disclosed where, under the proposed transaction, there would be a substantial capital reduction exercise which would entail a cash transfer of S$1.85 billion from Income to the proposed shareholders within three years upon completion of the transaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: While such capital reduction exercises are not uncommon in corporate mergers and acquisitions transactions, it would not be acceptable in this context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And the reason is that at the time of corporatisation in 2022, Income enjoyed an exemption from section 88 of the CSA, where they were allowed to carry over the S$2 billion of surplus capital into the corporate entity, rather than transfer it to the Co-operatives Societies Liquidation Account (CSLA) to benefit the wider co-op sector.

sections.label: Government halted proposed transaction
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill letting the MAS Minister withhold approval based on MCCY advice, after the Government halted the transaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In a way, I am glad that the Government, both MCCY and MAS, through its detailed assessments and due diligence, picked up this serious implication and intervened to halt this proposed transaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I support this Bill to allow the Minister in-charge of MAS to withhold the approval, based on the advice of MCCY, in which the considerations may be non-prudential in nature.

sections.label: Foreign acquisitions and market forces
sections.summary: The speaker cites past foreign acquisitions, welcomes the Government's open handling, and notes the market's limits and the Government's interventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Over the years, we seen foreign acquisition of local companies, including iconic ones that today, still continues to be foreign owned like NOL, Raffles Hotel, our three large generation companies, SPC, CPG, among others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is inconceivable for Singapore as a global business hub to prevent or resist any change of ownerships of companies as these are all part and parcel of the market realisation and maximisation of enterprise value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government handled this matter in an open and transparent manner, with the Ministerial Statement on Monday to explain the Government's position and considerations and thereafter tabled this amendment to the Insurance Act so that we can have this debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We will leave it to the invisible hand of the market to sort things out, but we are also fully cognisant that there may be pitfalls and areas where unfettered free market may not always serve us well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And that is why we do see, from time to time, the Government’s visible hands in action, to rectify a situation or to plug a service gap when necessary.

sections.label: MAS prudential grounds evaluation
sections.summary: Minister Edwin Tong said MAS evaluated the offer on prudential grounds and saw no reason for concern.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Minister Edwin Tong explained on Monday that MAS had evaluated the offer on prudential grounds, consistent with its regulatory mandate and on that basis, it saw no reason for concern.

sections.label: MAS, MCCY information sharing timeline
sections.summary: Minister Chee Hong Tat said MAS was unaware of MCCY's considerations and MAS shared information with MCCY only in early August.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, on Monday, Minister Chee Hong Tat also indicated that MAS was: "not aware of MCCY's considerations when MCCY issued the section 88 exemption, and hence did not link the proposal from Allianz to the exemption that MCCY had provided earlier".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, it was revealed on Monday that MAS had belatedly shared information with MCCY only in early August, after many Members of Parliament had raised questions related to the proposed transaction during the 6 August Sitting.

sections.label: Alternative capital sources for Income
sections.summary: The passage suggests other homegrown sources such as institutional investors or Temasek as alternative patient capital if Allianz's injection dilutes Income's brand equity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If Allianz's capital injection cannot be obtained with an assurance that it will not excessively dilute Income's brand equity, perhaps we can look to other homegrown sources such as a syndicate of institutional investors or even to our Sovereign Wealth Funds such as Temasek as alternative sources of patient capital.

sections.label: SIRA not triggered for Income
sections.summary: The passage questions why SIRA was not triggered given Income's DSII status and notes listed entities relate to security and military-industrial complex.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, one is also left to wonder why the Significant Investments Review Act, or SIRA, was not triggered in this case, given Income's status as a DSII.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, what does appear on the list all seem to be related in some form or fashion with security and the military-industrial complex.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But given how we have six whole pillars for Total Defence in Singapore, including economic, social and digital, it seems somewhat inconsistent with our own characterisation of defence that systematically important financial institutions such as DBS or digital assets such as Singtel could be sold without similar protections.

sections.label: Expected coordination among authorities
sections.summary: The passage states one would expect close coordination among authorities such as MCCY and MAS at all stages of evaluation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Due to the nature and the valuation of this deal, one would expect close coordination among the relevant authorities, such as MCCY and MAS, at all stages during the process of evaluation.

sections.label: Sharing information earlier with House
sections.summary: The passage asks whether information could have been shared earlier with the House when the topic was debated in August.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is comforting to know that we continue to have good officers in MAS and even the Civil Service, who are alert and can pick out issues beyond their scope.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, could this information not have been shared earlier with the House when the topic was heavily debated in Parliament back in August?

sections.label: Other businesses needing similar amendments
sections.summary: Asks whether other businesses like co-operatives, public charter institutions or critical infrastructure operators may need similar legislative amendments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would there be other businesses, which are organised as co-operatives, institutions of public charter or critical infrastructure operators, such as telecommunications companies, water desalination plants or oil refineries, which may require similar legislative amendments in order to prevent something similar from taking place?

sections.label: Clause 2 retrospective application
sections.summary: Refers to clause 2, proposed section 33A subsection 9, applying the section to relevant applications pending at commencement of the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For this, I specifically refer to clause 2 of the Bill which contains the proposed section 33A subsection 9 of the Act which states that, quote, this section also applies to a relevant application received by the authority before the commencement of the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2024 that is still pending as of that date.

sections.label: Offering circular long stop date
sections.summary: States that the offering circular's long stop date was nine months after the announcement date, reaching into next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, according to the offering circular, the long stop date was actually nine months after the announcement date, which would actually have taken us until sometime next year.

sections.label: Concerns about retrospective blocking legislation
sections.summary: Asks how the Government will address concerns that future parties' live transactions may be blocked by urgent retrospective legislation pending regulatory approvals.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How specifically does the Government hope to address concerns that future parties may have about the risk that their live transactions may suddenly find themselves blocked by urgent retrospective legislation being passed in the middle of a live transaction after an announcement is made in accordance with applicable listing rules and takeover codes and is just pending regulatory approvals?

sections.label: Income's corporatisation surplus representations
sections.summary: Notes the MCCY Minister's Statement shows blocking the transaction rested on Income's representations at corporatisation about keeping a substantial surplus of some S$2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, from the MCCY Minister's Statement, it is evident that one important consideration behind the Government's decision to block the transaction as currently structured, was based on representations that Income made at the time of its corporatisation as to why it should be allowed to keep a substantial surplus of some S$2 billion.

sections.label: WP abstention on the Bill
sections.summary: WP supports blocking the acquisition on public interest grounds and will not reject the Bill, but abstains over rushed retrospective legislation and legal certainty concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To conclude, WP supports the Government's blocking of the proposed acquisition in its current form on public interest grounds based on publicly available information, especially given the concerns that my colleagues and I had raised in this Chamber in August.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will not be rejecting the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, we believe that the downsides to whether this Bill will be seen to be rushed and retrospective legislation-making, and this assault on legal and regulatory certainty that changing legislation in the middle of a major live transaction means that we would need to register our abstention on this Bill.

sections.label: Insurance Bill expanded diligence process
sections.summary: The Bill applies an expanded diligence process to MAS applications from three categories of licensed insurers and empowers the Minister to withhold approval on public interest grounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Insurance (Amendment) Bill would thus apply an expanded diligence process on applications to the MAS where the licensed insurer in the application falls under one of three categories: it is a co-operative; or it has acquired the principal business of a co-operative; or it has a substantial shareholder or effective controller which is a co-operative.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specifically, the new section 33A in the Bill would empower the Minister to withhold approval of application from the above categories of licensed insurers on grounds of public interest.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 33A also empowers the Minister to attach conditions to the approval and allows the Minister to add to, vary or revoke any of these conditions.

sections.label: PSP welcomes stopping Income-Allianz deal
sections.summary: PSP is heartened that the Government intervened to stop the proposed sale of a majority stake in Income Insurance to Allianz.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) is heartened that the Government has intervened to stop the proposed deal to sell a majority stake in Income Insurance to Allianz.

sections.label: Clarification on amending Insurance Act
sections.summary: The question asks the Government to clarify why amending the Insurance Act is necessary to stop the transaction instead of relying on existing provisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Government clarify why it is necessary to amend the Insurance Act to stop this transaction instead of relying on existing provisions?

sections.label: Capital reduction contradicts sale rationale
sections.summary: Statements about financial and non-financial institutions support the perception that more capital was the main reason for the sale, but the plan to reduce capital by S$1.85 billion contradicts this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: They have looked at financial institutions and non-financial institutions, locally and foreign.” All these statements contribute to the perception that the need for more capital is the number one reason for the sale of Income Insurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the plan to reduce capital by S$1.85 billion totally contradicts this argument.

sections.label: PSP relieved at blocked acquisition
sections.summary: In Mandarin, PSP states it is relieved that the Government has blocked the acquisition of Income by Allianz.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Deputy Speaker, PSP is relieved that the Government has blocked the acquisition of Income by Allianz.

sections.label: PSP seeks explanation, supports Bill
sections.summary: PSP says sections 26 and 27 already give MAS sufficient discretion, hopes for a detailed explanation of the Bill's necessity, and will support the Bill if necessary to stop the deal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In our view, sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act already gives the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) sufficient discretion to reject this deal based on factors beyond financial prudence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, PSP hopes that the Government can provide a more detailed explanation of the necessairty of this Bill today. : In closing, PSP agrees with the Government that it would be in the public interest to stop the deal from proceeding in its current form.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, despite our reservations about this urgent Bill, we will support this Bill if it is necessary to stop the deal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill is being proposed in light of the Income-Allianz deal which has raised important questions regarding public interest, corporate governance and the preservation of social missions within insurance entities, especially those transitioning from co-operative models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their joint review of the Income-Allianz transaction, announced on 17 July, revealed concerns that went beyond a typical business deal.

sections.label: Door open for negotiations
sections.summary: The door remains open for further negotiations if any future proposal addresses MCCY and MAS concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The door remains open for further negotiations, provided that any future proposal addresses the concerns raised by MCCY and MAS.

sections.label: Allianz Income capital extraction
sections.summary: Allianz committed to Income's S$100 million pledge, but Income and Allianz planned to return about S$1.85 billion cash to shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister of State Alvin Tan also emphasised how Allianz has committed to continue Income's pledge of S$100 million over 10 years from 2021, to provide social mobility among the lower income and support the well-being of seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But now we know that Income and Allianz had all along planned to return about S$1.85 billion in cash to its shareholders within the first three years of completing the transaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With the knowledge of the capital extraction, we can see that this deal was essentially an asset-stripping exercise in favour of the shareholders, especially NE and Allianz, with little consideration for the social mission and the interest of the 1.7 million policy-holders.

sections.label: Capital reduction prudential alarm
sections.summary: A capital reduction exercise should have raised alarm bells in MAS, given NE's capital injections of up to S$630 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In my view a capital reduction exercise should have raised alarm bells in MAS even from a prudential standpoint, especially given that NE has had to put in capital injections of about up to S$630 million over the years.

sections.label: Offer, capital reduction, MCCY doubts
sections.summary: The offer was called good for Income and policyholders, but includes a capital reduction plan and MCCY is not confident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: They added, "We believe the offer is good for Income, good for its policy holders and will enable us to fulfil our mission from a stronger position".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But now we know that the proposed transaction includes a capital reduction plan and MCCY, I quote, "is not confident that the proposed transaction would not affect the ability of the co-op movement as a whole or of Income itself to carry out its social mission".

sections.label: NE relinquishing control concerns
sections.summary: NE relinquished control of Income to Allianz with little assurance, so policyholders may be concerned about safeguards for surpluses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And if NE had agreed so easily to relinquish control of Income to Allianz with so little assurance about the ability of Income to carry out its social mission, it is arguably justifiable for policy-holders to be concerned whether in a future deal there will be safeguards to protect the surpluses in the policy funds accruing to the policy-holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, contrary to what the NTUC leaders have represented to Singaporeans, we can say that this transaction is not good for Income, not good for its policy-holders and will not allow Income to continue to fulfil its social mission.

sections.label: Cabinet Ministers information responsibility
sections.summary: Cabinet Ministers are responsible for ensuring they are apprised of all relevant information before making decisions and public pronouncements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Or to put it simply, the left hand does not know what the right hand is doing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is the responsibility of Cabinet Ministers to ensure that they are apprised of all relevant and important information and to consider that fully before making decisions and making public pronouncements.

sections.label: Minister's power over insurer transactions
sections.summary: The passage states the Minister may withhold approval of transactions involving co-operative-owned insurers when deemed necessary in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We hope that they will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It grants the Minister the authority to withhold approval of transactions involving co-operative-owned insurers where the Minster deems it necessary in the public interest.

sections.label: Income's regulatory compliance acknowledged
sections.summary: The Ministerial Statement on Monday said the Government acknowledged Income complied with regulatory obligations by fully disclosing its plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Ministerial Statement on Monday, the Government has acknowledged that Income complied with regulatory obligations by disclosing their plans fully.

sections.label: Possible amendments over corporatised co-ops
sections.summary: The Ministerial Statement on Monday highlighted that MCCY may consider future legislative amendments giving the Government stronger levers over co-ops wishing to corporatise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Ministerial Statement on Monday highlighted that MCCY may consider future legislative amendments to give the Government stronger levers over co-ops that may wish to be corporatised.

sections.label: Essentials for trust and cooperation
sections.summary: The passage states clear definitions of public interest, guidelines, early discussions on deal-breaking concerns and confidentiality protection are essential to trust and cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clear definitions of public interest, guidelines, early discussions on deal-breaking concerns and the protection of confidentiality are essential to fostering an environment of trust and cooperation.

sections.label: Impact on business certainty
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister considered the legislation's impact on business certainty and Singapore's regulatory environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, has the Minister considered the impact that the enactment of this legislation will have on business certainty and the regulatory environment in Singapore?

sections.label: Re-evaluation and message to world
sections.summary: The passage says the Government re-evaluated when new facts emerged, but warns against signalling that corporate deals can be suddenly overturned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has been courageous enough to take a step back and re-evaluate the situation, when new facts were revealed – this is something that is admirable – and it is important to acknowledge the relevance of this and the fact that this was done quickly when the Government realised that new information was in its hands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, we need to be careful that we are not inadvertently sending a message to the world at large, that it is possible for corporate deals to be suddenly overturned by the Government, for legislation to be rushed through and for carefully planned corporate negotiations to be disrupted.

sections.label: MAS interpretation of prudent business
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to explain MAS' understanding of the term "conduct its business prudently" in the Insurance Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister be able to explain further MAS' understanding and interpretation of the term "conduct its business prudently", as it is set out in sections 26(2)(b) and 27(3)(b) of the Insurance Act?

sections.label: Government blocked Income deal
sections.summary: The Government stopped the deal because there were no binding provisions for Income's social mission and a S$1.85 billion capital extraction plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On Monday, it therefore came as a surprise to many Singaporeans that the Government had intervened to stop the deal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note in MCCY's assessment, as articulated by Minister Edwin Tong, that one of the two key reasons why the deal was not approved in its current form, was because there were, and I quote, "no clear binding provisions or structural protections in the deal to ensure that Income's social mission will be discharged." It is now clear that the promises around Income's commitment to maintaining its social mission are not legally binding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The other key reason why the proposed transaction was blocked, pertains to the proposed capital extraction plan, a substantial amount of about S$1.85 billion over three years.

sections.label: Minister approval for insurer control
sections.summary: The amendment introducing section 33(a) requires the Minister's approval before MAS may approve applications for effective control or substantial shareholding of licensed insurers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister could address this point with clarity and transparency, so that Singaporeans can better understand and fully appreciate the deliberations of the Government, especially when it concerns national assets to which Singaporeans have deep emotional ties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is important in the context of this Bill, as the amendment introducing section 33(a) into the Insurance Act will now require the Minister's approval before the MAS may approve an application by a person to obtain effective control of or become a substantial shareholder of certain licensed insurers.

sections.label: Minister decides on co-operative insurers
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new section allowing the Minister to approve or reject applications involving co-operative insurers based on public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, this Bill introduces a new section that allows the Minister to approve or reject applications involving co-operative insurers based on what is considered "public interest".

sections.label: Minister vetoes sales or acquisitions
sections.summary: The Bill grants the Minister authority to decide or veto sales or acquisitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill grants the Minister authority to decide or veto sales or acquisitions.

sections.label: Impartial appeals process for decisions
sections.summary: An impartial appeals process should be implemented to ensure fair decisions, and Allianz reportedly agreed to consider revising its offer to Income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And fourth, we should implement an impartial appeals process to ensure that decisions are fair and inspire confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am also glad to see that it was reported that Allianz has agreed to consider revising its offer to Income after the current deal was prevented by the Singapore Government.

sections.label: Income shareholders Allianz payout
sections.summary: Income's shareholders, with Allianz as majority, would receive some S$1.85 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Income’s shareholders, of which Allianz would be the majority amongst, would receive some S$1.85 billion.

sections.label: Section 88 exemption surplus transfer
sections.summary: The Minister granted Income an exemption under section 88 of the CSA, allowing about S$2 billion of surplus to be carried over instead of going to the CSLA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a matter of public interest because, along with the corporatisation, the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth had also granted an exemption to Income under section 88 of the CSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This allowed Income to carry over approximately S$2 billion of surplus to the new entity, instead of it being distributed to members and, importantly, the surplus being transferred to the CSLA, which is applied for the benefit of the co-op sector generally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means that monies that ought to have gone to a public fund have been denied.

sections.label: Income representations to MCCY
sections.summary: Income represented to MCCY in June 2022 that corporatisation would make it a more attractive proposition to investors and strategic partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How involved were they and the senior management of Income in, on the one hand, making representations to MCCY and, on the other, arranging the deal with Allianz?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note, in particular, that Income made the following representation to MCCY in June 2022 that: “We believe that, pursuant to corporatisation, the Co-op", that is, Income, "will be regarded to offer a more attractive proposition to investors and strategic partners.

sections.label: Government require Income explain structure
sections.summary: Given the exemption was premised on difficulty competing and fulfilling its social mission, the Government should require Income to explain how it will use its corporate structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, Sir, given that Income’s move to corporatise which included the exemption under section 88 was premised on it finding it difficult to compete and to fulfil its social mission, I think it is important that the Government require Income to explain how it is going to leverage on its current corporate structure to do so, given that the Allianz deal may be off.

sections.label: Minister approval of Income-Allianz deal
sections.summary: The question asks whether after the Bill the Income-Allianz deal would be subject to the Minister's approval and then not approved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would it be that, after the passing of this Bill, that the Income-Allianz deal would be subject to the Minister’s approval and that the Minister would then not approve?

sections.label: Divestment off table, NE proceeds
sections.summary: The majority stake divestment in Income will be off the table with the Bill's passage, and NE would receive divestment proceeds and a capital extraction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposal for the divestment of a majority stake in Income will now be off the table with the passage of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Details that surfaced on Monday disclosed that NE would receive both the proceeds from the proposed divestment and a subsequent capital extraction, thus freeing up funds which could be deployed for continuing the broader social mission, presumably beyond Income.

sections.label: Public listing of Income
sections.summary: The passage asks that the option of a public listing of Income as a profitable and socially responsible business be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, consider the option of a public listing of Income as a profitable and socially responsible business.

sections.label: NE as social benchmark
sections.summary: The passage states NE can be the national benchmark for a socially-driven organisation and cites its annual report showing healthy finances and social initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NE can be the national benchmark for a model socially-driven organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Doing well can, therefore, be more clearly articulated for NE, which, going by the latest annual report, demonstrates a healthy financial state and a commendable list of impactful social initiatives for Singaporeans.

sections.label: MAS approval not given
sections.summary: The passage states Minister Edwin Tong announced the Government's view against the transaction in its current form, and MAS approval has not been given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While Minister Edwin Tong has announced the Government's view that it would not be in the public interest for the transaction to proceed in its current form, the fact remains that the requisite MAS approval has not yet been given for the deal to proceed.

sections.label: Income social purpose bar
sections.summary: The passage states the bar is lower than national security interests under SIRA, and Alvin Tan said Income's social purpose is unlikely to meet SIRA's high bar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What we do know is that it is a lower bar than the "national security interests" protected under the Significant Investments Review Act (SIRA), when Minister of State Alvin Tan replied to me that Income’s "social purpose" is unlikely to meet the high bar to be protected under SIRA.

sections.label: MAS consultation and exemption conditions
sections.summary: The passage states Chee Hong Tat explained MAS did not consult MCCY before the 6 August 2024 Parliamentary Questions, and asks about conditions on Income's exemption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Minister Chee Hong Tat explained that it did not occur to MAS to consult with MCCY, particularly on Income's previous exemption from section 88 of the CSA, before the Parliamentary Questions of 6 August 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is understandable because it is not an issue that would arise in most applications made to MAS for approval, which would not relate to co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, my question is whether any conditions were attached to the exemption for Income to carry over S$2 billion of accumulated surplus to its new corporate form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Instead of enacting the amendment in this proposed Bill, would MCCY not be able to exercise effective regulation by imposing relevant conditions in the exemption that was given, for example, that any subsequent change of ownership must be cleared with MCCY, or that the carried-over surplus of S$2 billion had to be returned to the CSLA if certain prescribed events occurred?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On that note, can MCCY still vary the conditions of that exemption today?

sections.label: Amendment on co-op insurers
sections.summary: The passage states the amendment lets MAS consider the co-ops Minister's views to withhold approval for control of a co-op-linked insurer, and supports the Government's decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed amendment will allow MAS to consider the views of the Minister charged with the responsibility for co-ops to withhold approval for an application to obtain effective control or to become a substantial shareholder of an insurer that is a co-op or linked to a co-op, if it is in the public interest to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the reasons set out in the Ministerial Statement by Minister Edwin Tong on 14 October 2024, I support the Government’s decision that it is not in the public interest for the Income-Allianz deal in its current form to proceed.

sections.label: Scoped urgent Insurance Act amendments
sections.summary: The urgent Bill's amendments are scoped narrowly to a licensed insurer under sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act that is a co-operative or linked to one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, as this is an urgent Bill, it is appropriate that the proposed amendments are scoped and not broad-based so as not to impact the larger insurance market in Singapore or cause undue anxiety amongst insurers in an already regulated sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I support that the amendment is specific and applies only to a licensed insurer that is the subject of an application under sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act and where the licensed insurer is a co-operative or linked to a co-operative.

sections.label: NTUC CC not told capital reduction
sections.summary: NTUC CC was briefed by NE and Income on the deal's strategic imperatives but was not told of the capital reduction plan.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Specific to this transaction, NTUC CC was briefed by NE and Income on the strategic imperatives for the deal and did not highlight to CC, the capital reduction plan.

sections.label: Income and NTUC social donations
sections.summary: Income pledged $100 million over 10 years from 2021, and NTUC social enterprises donated nearly $300 million over the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Income pledged $100 million over the next 10 years from 2021 to provide social mobility among the low-income and support the well-being of our seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Over the past 10 years, NTUC social enterprises, including Income, did much for the social good of Singapore through donating nearly $300 million to support the charitable works of NTUC Foundation, Bright Horizons Fund, Health for Life Fund, NTUC Education and Training Fund, NTUC-U Care Fund and Income Orange Aid.

sections.label: Income to study Ministerial Statement
sections.summary: Income will study the Ministerial Statement and Insurance Act amendments, while MCCY decided the transaction would not be in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Income has committed to study carefully, the implications of the Ministerial Statement by Minister for MCCY and the amendments of the Insurance Act and will work closely with the relevant stakeholders to decide on the next course of action.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: From the outset, NTUC's objective was to build a stronger Income so that it can do well and it can do good.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement, which includes NTUC and the enterprises, are united in our purpose and we will continue to do right by our people and what is necessary for the longer-term interest to serve workers and the people of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As I have explained on Monday, MCCY was given information, which it reviewed, looked at carefully and decided that it would not be in the public interest to allow this transaction to proceed.

sections.label: Ministerial Statement and Allianz suitability
sections.summary: The Government made a Ministerial Statement and tabled the Bill, and has no concerns over Allianz's standing or suitability to acquire a majority stake in Income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There is price-sensitive information, market-sensitive information, but the moment we were aware as to what steps we were going to take, how we proposed to take them, we came here, made a Ministerial Statement and explained fully, and then tabled the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have made it clear that the Government does not have concerns over Allianz's standing or suitability to acquire a majority stake in Income.

sections.label: MAS considering MCCY views
sections.summary: The Bill was framed because the Insurance Act has no provision explicitly allowing MAS to consider MCCY's views for an insurer that is a co-op or linked to one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, we framed this Bill because we acknowledge that under the Insurance Act today, there is no provision explicitly which allows MAS to consider the views of MCCY in the case of an application relating to an insurer that is either a co-op or linked to a co-op.

sections.label: Income social mission concerns
sections.summary: Government was not comfortable that Income could carry on its social mission after the transaction, citing capital reduction, no ring-fencing and ceding majority control.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: What we do know is, in this present arrangement, for the reasons I have set out, which I will briefly summarise in a moment, we were not comfortable that after this transaction, given the context in which it was done, that Income would be able to carry on with its social mission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The reasons we came round to this view, if I may reiterate, were the capital reduction occurring so soon after the exemption, the amount that was involved, the fact that there was no arrangement within the terms of the present transaction which would safeguard or ring-fence the advancement of Income's social mission, nor were there any structural protections in the terms of the proposed transaction that would allow us to have comfort that its social mission would be protected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We were also not clear what other adjustments or changes Income might be able to make thereafter to its portfolio, whether it would serve this area of underserved in the insurance business, trim its portfolio, change it altogether or reduce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, cumulatively, these factors, taken in the context of this transaction, where Income would cede majority control, were the reasons why we felt in this case this was not acceptable.

sections.label: Reinsurance and capital adequacy
sections.summary: Reinsuring part of Income's portfolio removes liabilities, improving its capital adequacy ratio, so MAS was satisfied the new entity would still meet its ratios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On that basis, this arrangement allows for Income to reinsure part of its portfolio of risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And the moment it is able to reinsure that portfolio of risk, it would not have to maintain that level of capital to meet the capital adequacy ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in that context, even in the proposed plan for a capital reduction to take place, if you have a portion of the portfolio that has been reinsured and taken off your liability books, that will contribute towards a more healthy and positive capital adequacy ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I do not have details and specifics of the numbers and the plans, but that is the principle on which this was done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is why we are able to say, as I did on Monday, that after evaluating the capital optimisation plan, MAS was satisfied that despite the capital reduction taking place, Income, the new entity, would still be projected to meet all its capital adequacy ratios with a healthy margin.

sections.label: Bill scope and MAS approval
sections.summary: The Bill is urgent and scoped to co-operative insurers, letting the Minister-in-charge of MAS consider MCCY's views and withhold approval in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: During these consultations, MAS would incorporate relevant feedback and address concerns that arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This Bill is an exception due to its urgency, because the deal with Allianz is under consideration by shareholders, and it is tightly scoped to co-operative insurers, insurers that have assumed the business of a co-op, or have a substantial shareholder or effective controller that is a co-op.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As there is currently no provision in the Insurance Act which allows MAS to consider the views of MCCY in the case of an application relating to an insurer that is either a co-op or linked to a co-op, the proposed amendments would allow the Minister-in-charge of MAS to consider the views of the Minister responsible for the administration of the CSA and to withhold approval involving such applications if the Minister-in-charge of MAS considers that it is in the public interest to do so.

sections.label: Open to new deal
sections.summary: The Government decided the transaction in its current form should not proceed but is open to NE working out a new deal addressing MCCY's concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As highlighted in Minster Edwin Tong's Ministerial Statement, while the Government has decided that it would not be in the public interest for the transaction, in its current form, to proceed, we are open for NE to work out a new deal, whether with Allianz or another entity, which can address MCCY's concerns.

sections.label: MAS Board not informed
sections.summary: MAS did not surface the information to its Board before the 6 August Parliament Sitting, and the Government then found the deal not in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As the MAS team was still assessing the proposal, they did not surface this information to the MAS Board before the 6 August Parliament Sitting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government then reached a view that it was not in the public interest for the deal in its current form to proceed.

sections.label: Cabinet decided against deal
sections.summary: The Cabinet decided it could not allow the deal in its current form to proceed, which is why the Bill is brought to Parliament for approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Leong asked who should be in charge?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is the Cabinet that decided that we could not allow the deal, in its current form, to proceed and that is why we are bringing this Bill to Parliament for approval.

sections.label: Income deal not allowed
sections.summary: The Government concluded it would not allow the deal to proceed, though it wanted Income strengthened to serve policy-holders and its social mission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They wanted to strengthen Income, so that Income is in a stronger position to serve its policy-holders and also to fulfil its social mission, because to do good, you must first do well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We may have differences in views, as Minister Edwin Tong mentioned earlier, with regard to this deal, whether this deal is something that the Government would allow to proceed and we have come to the conclusion that we would not allow this deal to proceed.

sections.label: Bill gives Minister MAS power
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Minister-in-charge of MAS consider the CSA Minister's views on applications for effective control or substantial shareholding of a licensed insurer that is a co-op.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That would not be fair to our sisters and brothers from NTUC and NE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And we do not want the deal in its current form to go through.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Bill will allow the Minister-in-charge of MAS to consider the views of the Minister charged with the responsibility of the CSA in applications to obtain effective control or become a substantial shareholder of a licensed insurer that is a co-op, has acquired the business of a co-op or has a substantial shareholder or effective controller that is a co-operative.

sections.label: Transaction cannot proceed as proposed
sections.summary: The Government determined the proposed transaction cannot proceed in its current form but supports NE and Income seeking a strong partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government has determined that this proposed transaction cannot proceed in its current form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: However, we remain supportive of NE's and Income's efforts to look for a strong partner, including with Allianz or another entity, to strengthen Income's capital base and market position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government recognises and agrees that Income must do well before it is able to continue doing good on a sustained basis.

sections.label: SIRA designated entities questioned
sections.summary: A speaker says no satisfactory reason was heard why SIRA designated entities are limited to the military and industrial complex.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Accepting that we do not wish to list every possible Singapore firm under SIRA, I still have not heard a satisfactory reason as to why the designated entities are limited to only those within the military, industrial complex, whereas our Total Defence pillars clearly go into financial and digital elements.

sections.label: SIRA and sectoral regulators
sections.summary: SIRA concerns national security, and DBS and Singtel are covered by sectoral regulators MAS and IMDA as gatekeepers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: With regard to SIRA, I have already explained earlier that this has to do with national security and I also mentioned in my reply that we will also look at whether there are other Acts that cover some of these entities; and if there are, then there is no need to replicate this with SIRA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the two examples that Assoc Prof Lim kept raising, DBS and Singtel, I have already explained that there are sectoral regulators – in the case of DBS, it will be MAS; in the case of Singtel, it will be IMDA – that would play the role of the gatekeeper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And if you want to acquire shares in DBS or in Singtel that goes beyond a certain percentage, you do need the regulator's approval before you are allowed to do so.

sections.label: Cabinet decided to bring Bill
sections.summary: After the 6 August Sitting, agencies and Ministers discussed information from MAS, and Cabinet decided to bring the Bill to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Indeed, that is why, after the 6 August Sitting, when MCCY received the information from MAS, the agencies then got together, the Ministers then got together and discussed, and eventually, Cabinet made a decision to bring this Bill to Parliament.

sections.label: Allianz capital reduction application
sections.summary: No application was made by Allianz on the capital reduction; only a preliminary business plan was submitted in mid-July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: From a prudential point of view, is this something that we would be prepared to consider?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But as I mentioned earlier in my closing speech, there was no application by Allianz on the capital reduction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They only submitted a preliminary business plan in mid-July.

sections.label: MAS powers and MCCY views
sections.summary: Sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act lack an explicit provision for MAS to consider MCCY views on social mission, and the proposal is urgent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Second, the point about why MAS does not have the powers, I have also explained this, that in the existing sections 26 and 27 of the Insurance Act, there is not an explicit provision under the Insurance Act for MAS to take into account the views of MCCY, which will include questions relating to social mission in assessing a proposed acquisition of an insurer with co-operative links.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, we cannot rely on the existing provisions without this set of amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And because it is a proposal that is under consideration by shareholders, there is urgency.

sections.label: Clarification on pending applications
sections.summary: Ms He asks whether new section 33A(9), covering pending applications, refers to this transaction or another.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: In relation to my clarification for the Minister-in-charge of MAS, I think the Minister mentioned twice that there was no formal application made by Allianz in relation to this proposed acquisition of the majority stake in Income.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: I just wanted to ask some clarification because in the proposed new section 33A of the Act, in subsection 9, it states, and I quoted this in my speech actually, "This section applies also to a relevant application received by the authority before the date of commencement of the Insurance Amendment Act 2024 that is still pending as of that date." Can the Minister clarify whether this refers to this transaction or another transaction?

sections.label: Bill urgency
sections.summary: The Bill is urgent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The second point that Ms He raised, this Bill is urgent.

sections.label: Multi-Ministry task force suggestion
sections.summary: He suggested that future transactions of such strategic importance should at the outset involve a multi-Ministry task force.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The second point is that he had asked me to make a suggestion and I did so in my speech, for how I think we should go forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This is the constructive part and that is that future transactions of such strategic importance should at the outset involve the establishment of a multi-Ministry task force.

sections.label: Government openness with licensees
sections.summary: The Government prefers being open and transparent with licensees, coming to Parliament with the Bill rather than telling a company to back off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Along the way, because they were submitting business plans, there were certainly discussions between MAS and Allianz on what they have submitted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I do want to make a point, Mr Deputy Speaker, that the Government, when it comes to dealing with our licensees and with industry players, we would like to take the approach of being open and transparent, and that if we have concerns with the deal, we have our reasons, we would rather do it in a manner like what we are doing now, come to Parliament with the proposed Bill, explain why we are doing it, rather than — and I hope that is not what Mr Leong is suggesting, because to go to the company and say, as a regulator, "I don't think you should be doing this and I think you should be backing off." I think if you do that, you may actually send more uncertainty and create more worries in the industry.

sections.label: Bill vote and Select Committee
sections.summary: The Ayes have it, and the Bill should ordinarily be referred to a Select Committee under Standing Order No 68.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Less those seven abstentions, everybody else has voted "Aye".

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I declare that the "Ayes" have it, the "Ayes" have it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Although the provisions of the Bill are drafted in general terms, it is clear from the Ministerial Statement by the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth on 14 October 2024 and from the Second Reading debate today, that the Bill is in substance, aimed at the proposed acquisition of the Income Insurance Limited by Allianz Europe BV.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Consequently, under the provisions of Standing Order No 68, the Bill should ordinarily after the Second Reading, be referred to a Select Committee.

sections.label: Seven abstentions in vote
sections.summary: Seven members abstained, and everyone else in the Chamber voted Aye.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Could I ask all those who are seeking to abstain to stand up in front of your seats?

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: There being seven abstentions, and notwithstanding the seven, everyone else in the Chamber has voted "Aye".
